highlights: Dynamic brain entropy over sliding windows, clustered by k-means into recurrent brain states, described by occupancy and dwell time.
The same measures then go to patient groups against matched controls.
Following up on published brain-state work from Dr. Xiaoqing Gao’s group.

research.name: Zhejiang University, in collaboration with Dr. Jianghao Liu, Paris Brain Institute (ICM)
highlights: Research content: using signal detection theory to study how imagination affects perception.

Design and methods: the protocol pairs a near-threshold perceptual detection task with an imagery task, plus electrophysiological and neuromodulation measures of visual-cortical and prefrontal involvement.
Role: built the experimental platform at Zhejiang University and was responsible for participant recruitment, data collection and analysis, and quality control.
Imaging studies are in preparation: a simultaneous fMRI–EEG study of where and when imagery enters perception, and a TMS–EEG study of whether the visual-cortical node is necessary.

research.name: Zhejiang University
research.position: Acquired Silent Reading Disorder: A Single-Case Study
highlights: Case: a 19-year-old who lost spontaneous inner speech after a month of “eye–mind direct” speed-reading practice (forced suppression of subvocalization plus forced acceleration), and could no longer understand text when reading silently without external support.

Experiments: a remote session (~2.5 h) with interview, YBOCS/VVIQ/BAIS, rapid automatized naming and five jsPsych tasks (three writing systems, RSVP, homophone judgement, manual Stroop, rapid identification); then an in-lab picture–text matching task over one to ten characters under five pacing conditions (no aid; 4, 2, 1 and 0.5 Hz).
Account I proposed: a learned gating deficit in auditory imagery — the generation is intact, but voluntary initiation is blocked, and external rhythm or movement can drive it.
Follow-up: he later recovered at a local hospital after low-frequency TMS over the right SMA, consistent with what the account predicts. Wish him well!
